record.body: Different habitats sound different, and comparing their soundscapes is a core soundscape-ecology method. A mature forest soundscape is layered: insects high, birds in the middle, mammals low, with wind in the canopy as geophony. A grassland soundscape is more open: wind dominates geophony, and bird and insect calls carry far. A wetland soundscape is dominated by water geophony and frog and bird biophony, often with the densest choruses of any habitat. The same three layers appear in all three habitats, but their balance differs, and that balance is itself ecological data: a forest whose canopy birds have vanished sounds different from an intact forest even before a surveyor arrives. This record covers all three layers, stated separately for each habitat, never blurred.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Habitat Soundscape Comparison: Forest, Grassland, and Wetland'
import math
BIO = 58
GEO = 48
ANTH = 40
tot = 10 * math.log10(10 ** (BIO / 10.0) + 10 ** (GEO / 10.0) + 10 ** (ANTH / 10.0))
dom = 'biophony' if BIO >= GEO and BIO >= ANTH else ('geophony' if GEO >= ANTH else 'anthrophony')
print('Record: ' + TITLE)
print('Biophony: %.1f decibels' % BIO)
print('Geophony: %.1f decibels' % GEO)
print('Anthrophony: %.1f decibels' % ANTH)
print('Combined soundscape level: %.1f decibels' % tot)
print('Dominant layer: ' + dom)
print('Layers are mixed in arithmetic but kept distinct in description.')
demo.expected_output:
Record: Habitat Soundscape Comparison: Forest, Grassland, and Wetland
Biophony: 58.0 decibels
Geophony: 48.0 decibels
Anthrophony: 40.0 decibels
Combined soundscape level: 58.5 decibels
Dominant layer: biophony
Layers are mixed in arithmetic but kept distinct in description.
